GREEN.label: Low factors found
GREEN.title: No major risk factors found right now
GREEN.text: Based on your answers, we didn't find strong kidney risk factors today. Keep up regular checkups, especially if your health changes.

AMBER.label: Kidney check recommended
AMBER.title: Kidney check recommended
AMBER.text: Your answers show some factors that can be associated with kidney disease. Consider discussing kidney screening with a healthcare professional.

RED.label: Please see a doctor soon
RED.title: Please see a doctor soon
RED.text: Your answers show several factors, or symptoms, worth having assessed by a doctor soon. This is not a diagnosis — a professional evaluation is the safe next step.

quiz.urgentBody: One or more of your answers, such as blood in urine, reduced urine, or swelling, are worth having checked promptly by a doctor.

band.normal: This is generally within the typical range for healthy adults, though it should still be read alongside your urine ACR and history.
band.mild: This is a mildly reduced reading. On its own, this doesn't confirm kidney disease — it's worth discussing with a doctor along with a urine ACR test.
band.moderate: This reading is below the typical range. It's important to discuss this with a doctor soon, along with your urine ACR and past results.
band.severe: This reading is significantly below the typical range. Please arrange to see a doctor or nephrologist promptly for a full assessment.

diet.title: My kidney diet
diet.stageHint: Ask your nephrologist which stage applies to you if you're not sure — it's usually based on your most recent eGFR.
diet.basedOn: Based on {stage} and the foods you selected.
diet.moreFoods: Select a few more foods across categories to build a sample meal.
diet.disclaimer: Your plan is an educational guide based on the information you entered. Your nephrologist or dietitian may adjust it according to your lab results and medical condition.

classify.avoid: Not suggested at this CKD stage.
classify.normal: Allowed in normal amounts at the {stage} stage.
classify.highSodium: High sodium — best avoided or strictly limited at every CKD stage, for blood pressure and fluid control.
classify.highNutrientCkd3: Higher in {nutrient} — eat in smaller portions, and ask your dietitian if you eat this often.
classify.highNutrient: Higher in {nutrient} — best avoided at this stage unless your dietitian specifically approves it.
classify.friendly: Generally a kidney-friendly choice in normal portions.

doctor.title: Doctor tools
doctor.proOnly: For healthcare professional use. Not intended for patient self-assessment.
doctor.riskStratBody: KDIGO combines G category and A category to stratify risk of progression, cardiovascular events, and mortality — risk rises as GFR falls and/or albuminuria increases, independent of each other. Lowest risk sits at G1–G2 with A1; risk increases progressively toward G4–G5 and/or A3.
doctor.kfreNote: Validated for adults with CKD G3–G5 (eGFR <60) referred to nephrology. Derived in North American cohorts; a calibration factor is often applied outside North America. Use as one input among several for clinical decisions, not in isolation.
